alignments.note: Connective δέ rendered by the verse-opening *and*.
Inflected verb takes its supplied subject and the light-verb auxiliary under rules 7 and 9; rule 91 heads the unit on *regard*, the word carrying the ἐπιβλέπω sense, not on the empty *have*.
The English preposition governing the phrase realizes ἐπί under rule 36, not the verb *have regard*.
Substantival article before a participle supplies the pronoun and nothing else under rule 32; the relativizer stays with the participle.
Attributive participle recast as a finite relative clause; the relativizer is its helper under rules 7 and 32, headed on the lexical verb.
Article realized by *the* under rule 19.
Adjective λαμπράν → *fine*.
Noun stands alone, its determiner already on the preceding article s006 under rule 19; no case preposition is in question here, so rule 21 does not bear on it.
Second attributive article of τὴν ἐσθῆτα τὴν λαμπράν has no English realization; rule 23.
Coordinating καί → *and*.
Subjunctive rendered by the bare *say*; the subject is carried over from the preceding clause in the English.
Imperative κάθου → *Sit*.
Emphatic pronoun Σύ → *thou*.
Adverb ὧδε → *here*.

The adverb καλῶς is expanded into the frame *in a good place*; no Greek preposition is expressed for *in* to answer to, so the frame rides whole with the adverb. Rules 17 and 91 head it on *good*, the corpus spending *good*/*well* on this lexeme and *place* being the supplied generic completion. A head on *place* is the competing reading, rejected because rule 17 forbids choosing a word merely because it is the phrase's formal English noun.
Coordinating καί → *and*.
Inflected verb takes its supplied subject under rule 9, headed on the lexical verb.

Dative article carries its case preposition under rule 21, and under rule 49 it also takes the supplied nominal *man*, since its complement is the substantival adjective `πτωχῷ` and nothing else can carry the determiner — `τὸ τρίτον` → *the third part* gives *the … part* to the article. The unit is discontinuous under rule 15. Rule 22 then heads it on the nominal word and never on the determiner, so the head is *man*. Analysed as at JAS.2.6's `τὸν πτωχόν` → *the … man* under rule 24, and as JAS.1.11's `ὁ πλούσιος` → *the rich man* has it. Every corpus unit finalized since rule 49 entered the contract reads this shape the same way — twelve for the article and none for the adjective (1JN.2.13, 1JN.2.14, 1JN.2.20, 1JN.3.12, 1JN.3.22, 1JN.5.18, 1JN.5.19, 2CO.4.2, 2CO.5.17, JUD.1.15, JHN.17.15, JAS.1.11). Competing reading: leave the article a bare *to the* and give *poor man* to the adjective on rule 17's generic-noun clause; declined under rule 66's closing clause, which holds rules 22, 49 and 58 untouched where the supplied word answers to an article.

Substantival adjective left with a bare *poor*, the article beside it taking both the determiner and the supplied nominal *man* under rule 49. Rule 58's substantival-takes-the-determiner arm is not the case, an article being present; the anarthrous `πτωχός` → *a poor man* at JAS.2.2 is the contrast, where no article stood to take either word.
Imperative στῆθι → *Stand*.
Emphatic pronoun Σύ → *thou*.
Adverb ἐκεῖ → *there*.
Disjunctive ἤ → *or*.
Imperative κάθου → *sit*; the projection's gloss column is blank here, but the selected reading r01 of SBLGNT.JAS.2.3.v004 supplies the token and the ASV realizes it.
Preposition ὑπό → *under* under rule 36.
The genitive pronoun μου takes the English possessive, displacing the article's determiner; rule 20. μου carries no other English word, so this is rule 20 proper and not rule 76's availability arm.
Genitive pronoun realized by the possessive *my*.
Noun stands alone, the determiner slot being occupied by *my*.

review_notes: Reviewed against the token table: all 28 source and 35 target ids are partitioned exactly once, every head is a member of its own array, and both unrepresented units carry a valid source head with an empty target and null target head.

Substantive analysis was already correct and is unchanged. One note was corrected: s007's determiner sits on the accusative article s006 with no case preposition in play, so rule 19 and not rule 21 is what licenses it. The rule 21 citation on s017/s018 is correct, the dative article there genuinely carrying *to*.

Verified the two contract choices most likely to be challenged. ἐπί is expressed, so *to* on t005 belongs to the preposition under rule 36 rather than to a phrasal *have regard to*; and rule 91 heads s001 on *regard*, the word carrying the ἐπιβλέπω sense, against the empty support verb *have*.

s015 καλῶς → *in a good place* is the one head with a live competitor. Kept on *good* under rules 17 and 91, with *place* read as the supplied generic completion; the unit's note names *place* as the rejected reading so a later reader can act on it.

Two unrepresented units: the second attributive article s008 under rule 23, and s026 emptied by μου under rule 20. μου is free — it carries only *my* — so this is rule 20 proper, not rule 76's availability arm. A reference comparison expecting a *the* the ASV never wrote will report both as disagreements, and that report is not a correction.
τὸν φοροῦντα splits under rule 32 (article → *him*, participle → *that weareth*) rather than taking *him that* whole; rule 90 does not apply, the ASV writing two English words here.
